'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2022 Hadera shooting]]
**Two policemen are killed and 12 more people are injured during a [[mass shooting]] by two [[Islamic State]] gunmen at a bus stop in [[Hadera]], [[Haifa District]], [[Israel]]. The attackers are shot dead. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/two-suspected-arab-gunmen-wound-two-israeli-city-are-shot-dead-police-say-2022-03-27/ (Reuters)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/2-killed-in-suspected-terror-shooting-in-hadera-both-gunmen-also-killed/ (''Times of Israel'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[94th Academy Awards]]
**''[[CODA (2021 film)|CODA]]'' wins this year's [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]], while [[Jane Campion]] wins [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]] for ''[[The Power of the Dog (film)|The Power of the Dog]]''. [https://www.cnn.com/2022/03/27/entertainment/oscar-winners-2022/index.html (CNN)]
**[[Will Smith]] wins [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]] for his portrayal of [[Richard Williams (tennis coach)|Richard Williams]] in ''[[King Richard (film)|King Richard]]'', while [[Jessica Chastain]] wins [[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]] for her portrayal of [[Tammy Faye Messner]] in ''[[The Eyes of Tammy Faye (2021 film)|The Eyes of Tammy Faye]]''. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-03-28/will-smith-chris-rock-hit-oscars-2022/100944638 (ABC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/film/2022/mar/28/jessica-chastain-wins-best-actress-oscar-for-the-eyes-of-tammy-faye (''The Guardian'')]
**''[[Dune (2021 film)|Dune]]'' wins the most awards in six, mostly untelevised categories. [https://www.cheatsheet.com/entertainment/oscars-2022-how-many-academy-awards-dune-win.html/ (Showbiz Cheat Sheet)]
**''CODA'' star [[Troy Kotsur]] wins [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor|Best Supporting Actor]], becoming the first [[Hearing loss|deaf]] male actor to win an [[Academy Award]]. [https://variety.com/2022/awards/news/troy-kotsur-oscar-best-supporting-actor-coda-1235209964/ (''Variety'')]
** ''[[West Side Story (2021 film)|West Side Story]]'' star [[Ariana DeBose]] wins [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress|Best Supporting Actress]], becoming the first [[queer]] [[person of color|woman of colour]] to win an [[Academy Award]] [https://www.theguardian.com/film/2022/mar/28/ariana-debose-wins-best-supporting-actress-oscar-for-west-side-story (''The Guardian'')]
**Celebrities at the Awards wear blue and gold ribbons to stand in solidarity with [[Ukraine]] and pay tribute to the [[2022 Ukrainian refugee crisis|refugees]]. [https://amp.usatoday.com/amp/7186073001 (''USA Today'')] [https://www.thewrap.com/oscars-red-carpet-ukraine-support/amp/ (''The Wrap'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Wildfires in 2022]]
**[[Human rights in Ukraine|Ukrainian Human Rights]] [[Ombudsman in Ukraine|commissioner]] [[Lyudmyla Denisova]] warns that around 10,000 [[hectare]]s of [[forest fire]]s are currently burning near the [[Chernobyl Exclusion Zone]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/climate-change/news/chernobyl-ukraine-forest-fires-today-b2045021.html (''The Independent'')]
**A [[wildfire]] engulfs the uninhabited [[Gruinard Island]] in [[Gruinard Bay]], [[Scotland]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-highlands-islands-60892350 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Shanghai]]
*****[[Shanghai]] imposes a lockdown in the [[Pudong]] area and other parts of the city. Additionally, areas near the [[Huangpu River]] will undergo four days of [[COVID-19 testing]] beginning tomorrow. [https://amp.scmp.com/news/china/science/article/3172061/shanghai-orders-mass-pudong-lockdown-push-contain-covid-19-surge (''South China Morning Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Chief Executive of Hong Kong|Chief Executive]] [[Carrie Lam]] announces that [[Hong Kong]] will begin offering [[COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccinations]] at home for elderly people in the coming weeks in order to increase the vaccination rate. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-03-27/hong-kong-to-start-offering-covid-home-vaccinations-for-eldery (Bloomberg)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Reactions to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Russia–Ukraine relations]]
***Ukrainian delegate [[Davyd Arakhamia]] announces that in-person [[ceasefire]] [[Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|talks]] between the [[Ukrainians|Ukrainian]] and [[Russians|Russian]] delegations will occur in [[Turkey]]. The talks are expected to occur from March 28 to March 30. [https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/3441406-turkey-to-host-next-live-round-of-ukrainerussia-talks-on-march-2830.html (Ukrinform)]
*[[Nuclear program of Iran]]
**[[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Antony Blinken]] says that the [[United States|U.S.]] and their Gulf allies will deter [[Iran]] from acquiring a [[nuclear weapon]], regardless if a deal to revive the [[Iran nuclear deal|2015 agreement]] has been reached or not. [https://edition.cnn.com/2022/03/27/politics/blinken-iran-nuclear-deal/index.html?msclkid=3c7ff3afae4011ecac927c527b53a2a3 (CNN)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Protests against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[2022 anti-war protests in Russia]]
***Russian artist Yevgenia Isayeva douses herself in [[fake blood]] during an [[Anti-war movement|anti-war]] protest in [[Saint Petersburg]]. She is later detained by police. [https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-st-petersburg-protest-war/31773114.html (RFE/RL)]
*[[Crime in El Salvador]]
**[[El Salvador]] declares a [[state of emergency]] after 62 people were [[murder]]ed in the country yesterday, making it the most violent 24-hour period since the end of the [[Salvadoran Civil War|civil war in 1992]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-60893048 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2022 Uruguayan Law of Urgent Consideration referendum]]
**A [[referendum]] is held in [[Uruguay]] on whether to repeal the Urgent Consideration Law, which gives the [[Government of Uruguay|government]] more power to dismantle [[protests]] and increased security measures after record high [[crime rates]] in Uruguay in 2017. [https://en.mercopress.com/2022/03/27/polls-are-closed-in-uruguay-vote-count-begins-in-referendum-questioning-the-government (MercoPress)]
